t.E1505.agn: In 1984 JECFA set the ADI at 0–20 mg/kg body weight/day; when evaluating it as a flavouring substance in 1999 it maintained this value and saw no safety concern at current intake.
t.E1505.body: It is not expected to be absorbed unchanged; liver and blood enzymes break down triethyl citrate into citric acid and ethanol (more slowly in human blood than in rat blood).
t.E1505.found.1: Food supplement capsules and tablets (up to 3,500 mg/kg)
t.E1505.found.2: Carrier in flavourings (E 1505, E 1517, E 1518 and E 1520 combined, up to 3,000 mg/kg in food from all sources)
t.E1505.prod: Produced by esterifying citric acid with ethyl alcohol.
t.E1505.summary: A carrier produced from citric acid and ethanol. It is a foam stabiliser and solvent in egg white powder and flavourings.
t.E1505.what: The ethyl ester of citric acid; it is used as a carrier solvent and metal binder.
